text:
Camille: Pushed a tiny change to routing fallback logic earlier that affects how Hosted/Dedicated/Private rollbacks are observed. We need a quick sync on telemetry invariants and safe rollback paths.

Nate: Saw the deploy. What was the intent? I pulled a few traces and saw missing hosting.mode tags.

Camille: The intent was to prefer dedicated pools for warm tenants but fall back to hosted when capacity is tight. I realized we didn't carry a mode tag through the proxy so metrics couldn't separate a deliberate fallback vs an unexpected eviction.

Priya: That sounds risky for Private customers — fallback to hosted must be blocked by policy, not just config. Are we currently emitting a header that prevents fallback?

Camille: Not consistently. We have X-Redwood-Fallback: true/false in some adapters but the control plane doesn't enforce it when routes are congested.

Zoe: Can we enforce an invariant: hosting.mode ∈ {hosted,dedicated,private} must be attached to every request and every span. If hosting.mode==private then fallback must be rejected at the routing layer (HTTP 409 or a typed error) so apps get explicit failure instead of silent hosted fallback.

Nate: Agree. Also: telemetry needs a rollout_id + attempt_count to correlate retries/fallbacks across the whole request path. Right now we only have request_id.

Camille: Proposed minimal changes:
```
- plumbing: add header X-Redwood-Hosting-Mode -> upstream and all sidecars
- tracing: add tag hosting.mode & rollout_id & attempt_num to root span
- control plane: enforce fallback_allowed boolean per-tenant; deny fallback for private tenants
- metrics: emit fallback_reason tag on infra counters
```

Priya: +1. Two followups: how do we handle existing sessions where adapter doesn't speak the header? and sampling — we can't trace 100% of requests in prod.

Zoe: For legacy adapters we should have a short-lived compatibility window: controlplane will default to disallow fallback for tenants with policy private, and adapters missing header will get a soft-fail metric and be throttled into a compatibility audit stream (not instant block).

Nate: For sampling: sample 100% for any request that triggers a rollback/fallback path for 5m after the event, otherwise use normal sampling. Emit a high-cardinality debug event to the audit sink so SRE/product can replay sequences.

Camille: Sounds good. Also suggest adding header X-Redwood-Fallback-Allowed: false to preserve semantics (explicit opt-in). Router should respond with 409 + body {"code":"FALLBACK_BLOCKED","explain":"private tenant policy"} when fallback would be attempted.

Priya: What about unit/e2e tests? We need an infra test that simulates dedicated pool exhaustion and asserts no hosted traffic for private tenants (and asserts proper metrics emitted).

Camille: I'll add a test in eng-runtime/ci that uses the failpoint to exhaust capacity and checks no cross-env requests reach hosted endpoints for private tenants. Test should also assert metric: infra.fallback_attempt{reason="capacity",hosting_mode="private"} == 1 and that the request returned FALLBACK_BLOCKED.

Zoe: One more ops thing — add a rollout label to runtime logs: rollout_id=YYYYMMDD-{inc}. When we do a revert, we want to tie traces to the specific rollout so we can quickly compute delta-failure-rate.

Nate: Implementation note: make the header authoritative at the load-balancer layer (envoy filter) to avoid racey proxy translations. Envoy can also inject the rollout_id if missing and mark span as synthetic.

InfraBot: Automated check: existing routing rules with fallback:true will be flagged as part of the compatibility audit. See https://go/internal/routing/audit/1729456789 for list.

Camille: Action items: 1) I’ll open an RFC with the header/tracing fields + error contract. 2) Nate will draft envoy filter change. 3) Priya will add e2e tests and private-tenant policy enforcement. 4) Zoe will add rollout_id logging guidance.

Priya: Timeline? I can pick up tests tomorrow, hoping to land controlplane enforcement next week if RFC + filter are quick.

Nate: I’ll prototype the envoy filter today. Quick sketch:
```yaml
- name: set-hosting-mode
  match: request.headers["x-redwood-hosting-mode"] missing
  action: reject if tenant.policy.private == true
  else: inject header from tenant manifest
```

Zoe: Keep me looped for dashboard changes — I’ll add a new panel that compares fallback_rate{hosting_mode=private} vs hosted_latency after rollout.

Camille: Thanks all. I’ll kick off the RFC and link the infra audit. If anyone sees a security/regulatory hole with error bodies containing tenant ids call it out in the RFC — redact where necessary. :thumbsup:

Nate: 👍

Priya: Thanks — will follow up in the RFC comments.

Zoe: 👍 will scope dashboards after RFC lands.
